verdicts.title: Stop hooks force unbounded model continuations with no loop guard
verdicts.evidence: hooks-claude-code half CONFIRMED in current code: packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:269 still carries `TODO(stop-loop-guard): cap consecutive forced continuations; hooks must self-limit meanwhile`; the `agent/turn-stopping` listener (index.ts:270-277) steers on every merged deny with no counter, no Config field, and `stopPayload` (index.ts:345-347) hardcodes `stop_hook_active: false`. In agent-loop (packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts:408-412) turn-stopping fires inside the same turn's while loop and a steer re-populates inbox.nextStep, so each deny spends another model request in the same turn with no bound — an always-deny hook loops until abort. README.md:95 documents the gap verbatim ('the consecutive-block cap is not implemented (TODO(stop-loop-guard))... force-continues every step unless it self-limits'). Tests only cover a self-limiting hook (tests/coverage-cases.ts:212-241 use a marker file so the hook exits 0 on check 2); no deny-loop case exists. hooks-codex half REFUTED as of current code: packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts:167 + 350-366 implement a per-turn guard (`stopHookTurns` WeakMap, `stop_hook_active` reported live, second deny in the same turn warns 'remained blocking' and closes the turn), already covered by packages/hooks/hooks-codex/tests/bridge.spec.ts:160. The audit's cited codex line (src/index.ts:254) now holds the unrelated TODO(hook-continue-false). Remaining blast radius is therefore claude-code-only.
verdicts.corrections: The finding survives only for hooks-claude-code; hooks-codex already ships the loop guard (max one forced continuation per turn via the stop_hook_active flag) with a test. A per-turn cap is provably sufficient: turn-stopping fires at agent.ts:409 inside the same turn's loop and steer keeps the turn number constant, so `stopHookTurns.get(agent) === turn` correctly identifies the guard state across the forced continuation. Severity for the surviving half stays high (untrusted hooks.json deny-loop burns unbounded provider spend), but scope shrinks from two packages to one.
verdicts.fix_plan: Mirror the already-shipped codex guard into hooks-claude-code (root-cause fix, no shims, restores the symmetry AGENTS.md requires). In packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts: (1) add `const stopHookTurns = new WeakMap<Agent, number>()` beside `subagentChildren` (index.ts:125); (2) in the `agent/turn-stopping` listener compute `const stopHookActive = stopHookTurns.get(agent) === turn`, pass it into stopPayload (new param replacing the hardcoded `stop_hook_active: false` at index.ts:346), and on `merged.decision === 'deny'`: when stopHookActive, `ctx.logger.warn('hooks-claude-code: Stop hook remained blocking after its continuation in turn ' + turn + '; closing the turn')` and return without steering (wording mirrors hooks-codex/src/index.ts:356); otherwise `stopHookTurns.set(agent, turn)` then steer as today; (3) delete the TODO(stop-loop-guard) comment at index.ts:269 and update the block comment above the listener to state the once-per-turn contract. Update README.md line 43 (Stop row: blocking feeds reason through steer() once per turn; a still-blocking repeat closes the turn) and line 95 (stop_hook_active now reflects the guard; drop the cap TODO, keep the omitted-fields list; SubagentStop stays false per line 94). No new Config field: one forced continuation per turn is Claude Code's own stop_hook_active protocol semantics, identical to the codex bridge — not a deployment-varying tunable, so the no-hardcoded-tunables rule is not triggered (if a numeric cap beyond 1 is ever wanted, it becomes a validated Config field then). SubagentStop payload keeps stop_hook_active: false, matching codex. Non-trivial behavior change: include an Agent Note in the same PR.
verdicts.test_plan: Add two cases to the group === 'stop' section of packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/coverage-cases.ts (surfaced by the existing packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/coverage-stop.spec.ts runner, following the sh()/hooks()/marker conventions of lines 211-241). Case 1 (failing-first, terminates pre-fix): a Stop hook that appends its received stdin payload to a marker file, exits 2 on check 1 and 0 on check 2 — assert the second recorded payload has stop_hook_active === true (pre-fix it is false, so the assertion fails fast without hanging). Case 2 (failing-first, terminates pre-fix): a hook that exits 2 on checks 1-2 and 0 on check 3 — assert exactly 2 model requests (initial + one forced continuation) and that the 'remained blocking' warn fired; pre-fix the run makes 3 requests, so the count assertion fails while the test still terminates. No snapshot changes expected: no example snapshot pins the Stop hook payload flag (grep over examples/jsonrpc-agent and scripts/snapshots shows no stop_hook_active reference); package tests are the gate.
verdicts.risk: Behavior changes only for hooks whose Stop hook denies twice within one turn: the second deny now closes the turn instead of forcing another step. That is Claude Code's documented stop_hook_active contract and the codex bridge's shipped semantics, so the change is a parity fix, not a new policy. Hook-payload logs change (hook/invoked/result now record stop_hook_active: true on second same-turn checks) — the hook/result event schema already carries arbitrary output payloads, and the persisted field is bounded by the existing stderrSummaryMaxChars-style caps, so no SessionEventMap or persistence-format impact. Legitimate multi-block workflows can still force one continuation per turn across turns (the WeakMap keys on agent and compares turn numbers), so the cap cannot strand a task that makes progress across turn boundaries.

verdicts.corrections: Two adjustments to blast radius. (1) The finding detail also names 'concurrent RelayHarness.run 触发的隐式 start' — that path needs a second, adjacent guard the suggested_fix omits: RelayHarness.start (python/sdk/src/relay_harness/api.py:117-127) has its own unguarded `if self._initialized: return`, so fixing only HarnessClient still lets two concurrent runs both pass the harness check and send two `initialize` requests to the one spawned runtime (the second over-initializes a live agent). The minimal complete fix covers both layers. (2) Severity high is fair: this is the exact race class docs/defensive-patterns.md covers, and TS is immune only because the event loop serializes start().
verdicts.evidence: python/sdk/src/relay_harness/client.py:118-141 — `if self._proc is not None: return` (line 119) runs before `with self._lock` (line 121), the lock body only clears `_session_parents` and the two failure markers (lines 122-124), and `self._proc = subprocess.Popen(...)` (lines 130-139) plus `_start_reader_thread()`/`_start_stderr_thread()` (lines 140-141) all run after the lock is released. Two threads past the check both Popen; the second assignment overwrites the first handle while the orphan's reader/stderr threads keep reading it (`_reader_loop` captures `proc = self._proc` at line 403 — whichever thread reads first may even attach to the winner's proc, cross-wiring frames). The implicit-start path is real: RelayHarness.run → start_session → self.start() (api.py:134-144) and __enter__ (api.py:107). No guard elsewhere: python/sdk/tests/test_client.py has threading tests for concurrent writes (line 1171) and delivery races (lines 726, 731) but nothing covers concurrent start().
verdicts.fix_plan: 1) python/sdk/src/relay_harness/client.py `start()`: compute `args`/`env` (including `_inject_bundled_default_config`) before taking the lock, then `with self._lock:` re-check `if self._proc is not None: return`, clear `_session_parents`/failure markers, `Popen`, assign `self._proc`, then `_start_reader_thread()`/`_start_stderr_thread()` — keep the existing Popen→threads order inside the lock. Update the method's docstring with the thread-safety contract: concurrent start() calls spawn exactly one runtime. 2) python/sdk/src/relay_harness/api.py `RelayHarness.__init__`: add `self._start_lock = threading.Lock()`; `start()` becomes `with self._start_lock: if self._initialized: return; _client.start(); _client.initialize(...); self._initialized = True`. 3) Mention the single-spawn guarantee in python/sdk/README.md only if it already describes start()/threading (otherwise skip — no new doc surface).

Pre-computing args/env outside the lock keeps the `resolve_bundled_launch_args` package import off the lock path. Concurrent RelayHarness.start now issues initialize exactly once instead of possibly twice — strictly closer to the documented lifecycle. No wire or config changes; no snapshot impact.

verdicts.corrections: One correction to the suggested fix's guard set: the audit says 'when the pid is not alive (ESRCH) ... remove the stale lock' without a same-host check in the rank-14 text, but the R1 detail does say same-host. The lock file must therefore also record the owner host (today it stores only the pid, so a contender cannot tell a foreign-host lock from a local one). pid liveness needs the precise Node semantics: ESRCH proves death; EPERM means the process exists under another user and must be treated as alive (fail loud, not self-heal). Residual accepted window: pid reuse after a host reboot while an orphaned lock survives — documented, not engineered around (no zero-dep portable boot-id).
verdicts.evidence: packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:105-130 — withFileLock creates the lock with `writeFile(lockPath, `${process.pid}\n`, { flag: 'wx' })` (line 114), and on contention (isLockContention, lines 67-78) only backs off 20→200ms until `LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000` (lines 86-88, 110-124), then throws 'atomic-write: timed out waiting for the writer lock'. The pid in the file is never read; the JSDoc (lines 98-100) states 'orphan recovery is an operator action'. Nothing in the repo sweeps stale locks (grep for `.lock` readers returns nothing), so a process killed between line 114 and the `finally rm` (line 128) — kill -9, crash, power loss — leaves the lock forever and every future writer fails after a 2s retry storm. Blast radius is broader than the title says: withFileLock guards credentials-local (packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:394, 485 — every credential set/unset), settings-file (packages/settings/settings-file/src/index.ts:156, 215 — every settings patch), plus skill-inventory, preset/agent-presets, mcp-servers-file, and fs-local. packages/util/atomic-write/README.md:45 documents the operator-recovery stance, so the doc must change with the code.
verdicts.fix_plan: 1) packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts: change the lock payload to `${process.pid}\n${os.hostname()}\n` (add `hostname` from node:os; nothing else parses the payload — verified by repo grep, so the format change is safe). 2) In the contention branch, before backing off: `readFile(lockPath, 'utf8')`; parse pid (first line) and host (second line). Self-heal only when host matches `os.hostname()` AND `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws with `code === 'ESRCH'`: `rm(lockPath, { force: true })` and continue the retry loop immediately. Any other outcome — unreadable lock, malformed payload, foreign host, EPERM from kill, or the stale lock reappearing (another racer re-created it) — falls through to the existing backoff/deadline so the contender still fails loud with the timeout error. 3) Update the withFileLock JSDoc (replace the 'orphan recovery is an operator action' sentence with the self-heal contract: same-host, provably-dead owner pid; foreign-host or unreadable locks stay operator actions) and the module JSDoc if it names the protocol. 4) Update packages/util/atomic-write/README.md line 45 (Known Limitations bullet) to describe same-host stale-lock self-heal and the remaining operator cases; mirror in README.zh.md per the bilingual-doc convention. No Config field: LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS and the retry curve stay fixed protocol constants per the existing JSDoc rationale, and self-heal is a correctness property, not a deployment tunable. 5) Non-trivial change → include an Agent Note in the PR per AGENTS.md.
verdicts.risk: The behavior change only fires on the previously-permanent-failure path, so the safe direction is monotonic: today's outcome (timeout) remains the outcome whenever any ambiguity exists. The pid-reuse-after-reboot window is left failing loud (treated as a live lock) — same as today, never deletes a live writer's lock because a live pid returns success/EPERM from kill(pid,0). Hostname match confines self-heal to the local machine, protecting shared-filesystem deployments. Consumers (credentials, settings, presets, mcp-servers-file, fs-local) need no changes — they see only fewer lock timeouts.
verdicts.test_plan: packages/util/atomic-write/tests/atomic-write.spec.ts, inside the existing `describe('withFileLock')` (line 70, vitest `it(...)` convention), add three cases: (1) `it('recovers a stale lock whose recorded owner pid is dead on this host')` — spawn a short-lived child (`spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', ''])`), await its exit, pre-create `${file}.lock` with that pid + `os.hostname()`, then assert `withFileLock(file, op)` succeeds and op ran; this is the failing-first case (pre-fix it throws the timeout error). (2) `it('keeps timing out when the lock owner is alive')` — pre-create the lock with a live long-sleep child's pid; assert rejection with the timeout error and that the lock file still exists. (3) `it('keeps timing out when the lock records a foreign host')` — pre-create the lock with a dead pid + hostname 'rlh-foreign-host'; assert rejection. Case (2)/(3) pin the fail-loud boundary against over-eager self-heal.

verdicts.corrections: Two precision fixes. (1) The killable test is slightly narrower than stated: isSafeToKill (rlh.js:158-167) also excludes any image name containing 'electron' and the parent pid (isSelfPid covers process.pid AND process.ppid, rlh.js:154-156) — but unrelated node processes still pass, so the core claim stands. (2) process.kill(-pid) does not 'silently no-op': when the child is not a process-group leader the group signal throws ESRCH and the catch falls back to a single-pid SIGTERM (rlh.js:179-185) — net effect matches the finding (group-kill intent only partly real), but the mechanism is a caught-error fallback, not a silent no-op. (3) The httpReady gate requires the foreign server to answer HTTP 200 on GET / (probePort, rlh.js:352-369); a non-HTTP listener causes a port hop, so the dangerous case is specifically an HTTP server running on node — which is exactly the common dev-server case. Line drift since the audit is minor: killOwnedListeners now at rlh.js:284-298, httpReady fallback at 397-407, _doStop sweep at 908.
verdicts.evidence: apps/desktop/src/main/rlh.js:284-298 killOwnedListeners kills every listening pid whose image matches /^(node|rlh)(\.exe)?$/ (isSafeToKill, rlh.js:158-167) and is not self/ppid/electron. Two live call sites confirmed: (1) ensureOwnedPort rlh.js:397-407 — when the wanted port (default 3080, rlh.js:376; rlh.js:477,731; index.js:59) answers HTTP 200 (probePort rlh.js:352-369 only checks response.ok, no identity marker), it kills ALL node/rlh listeners on that port; the pid-file path (rlh.js:384-394) narrows only the first branch and the pid file is cleared at rlh.js:395 before the httpReady fallback runs. (2) RlhManager._doStop rlh.js:908 calls this._killOwnedListeners(this.port) unconditionally on every stop, even when no child or pid-file pid existed. Kill mechanism: taskkill /pid X /T /F on Windows (rlh.js:174-175, force-kills the whole descendant tree) or process.kill(-pid,'SIGTERM') group signal with single-pid fallback on POSIX (rlh.js:177-185). apps/desktop/src/main/index.js:61 shows ensureOwnedPort runs at every desktop boot via resolveLaunchTarget. No test guards against this: rlh.test.js only injects killOwnedListeners as a counting stub (rlh.test.js:127) and asserts it was called once on stop (rlh.test.js:420-444) — the opposite of a foreign-listener pin.
verdicts.fix_plan: Root cause: kill decisions lack an ownership proof. All edits in apps/desktop/src/main/rlh.js. (1) ensureOwnedPort (375-412): delete the probe.httpReady -> killOwnedListeners block (397-407); after the pid-file attempt an occupied port goes straight to the existing findFreePort hop (409-411). Rewrite the JSDoc (371-374) to state the contract: kills only the pid recorded in rlhd-web.pid and only while isSafeToKill; any other listener causes a port hop, never a kill. (2) _doStop (885-916): delete the unconditional this._killOwnedListeners(this.port) sweep (908-912) and its log line; the path already kills exactly child?.pid || this._readPidFile() (890, 905). (3) Delete now-dead code: listeningPids (250-282), killOwnedListeners (284-298), and the killOwnedListeners dep from the RlhManager deps table (comment line 463, default 491, accessor 961-963) — knip/hygiene would flag it otherwise; the repo's pre-release stance prefers deletion over stubs. (4) Make the group-kill intent real so our own child's descendants cannot linger and push the next boot onto a hopped port: in spawnHarness (314-322) pass detached: true on POSIX so the child leads its own process group and killTree's process.kill(-pid) reaches the whole tree (Windows unchanged: taskkill /T /F already covers descendants); JSDoc the spawn contract. No new Config field: the only tunable (port) is already config.port; PORT_SCAN_RANGE stays a fixed desktop constant. Write the required Agent Note in .agents/notes/ for the behavior change.
verdicts.risk: Behavior change: a genuinely owned leftover rlh whose pid file was lost now yields a port hop (desktop serves on 3081+, existing user-visible log at rlh.js:410) instead of a kill — safe by construction, and the pid-file path already covers the normal crash-leftover case since the pid file is written at spawn (761) and cleared only on stop/error. Stop no longer clears strangers from the port; foreign listeners are untouched. detached:true means the child no longer receives signals aimed at the desktop's process group — an Electron GUI main process has no controlling terminal, and child lifecycle is already managed explicitly via child.kill/killTree, so no regression path. A user who previously relied on the desktop sweeping a stray node process from 3080 will see a hop instead; that reliance was the bug.

(1) New test 'ensureOwnedPort：外部 node 监听不被击杀，跳端口': give ensureOwnedPort an injectable deps parameter (probePort/readPidFile/processAlive/killTree seams, the same pattern RlhManager already uses); inject a stale pid file (processAlive=false), a port answering 200, and a foreign listening pid (e.g. 9999) whose image is 'node'; assert the returned port is > wanted and killTree was never called with the foreign pid — fails on current code because the httpReady branch kills it. verdicts.evidence: apps/desktop/src/main/config.js:180-186 — `function readJson(file, fallback) { try { return { ...fallback, ...JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')) }; } catch { return { ...fallback }; } }` — a bare catch with no naming comment (violating the AGENTS.md empty-catch rule), no log, and no distinction between ENOENT (expected first launch) and a parse failure of an existing file. loadConfig (config.js:211-236) then merges DEFAULTS over the empty result: a corrupt config.json resets workspace (via the `!config.workspace` → defaultWorkspace() branch at line 227-229), theme, locale, simpleMode, restart policy; a corrupt credentials.json (read at line 213) resets apiKey/baseUrl/githubToken/remoteToken to stored-or-empty. saveConfig (config.js:238-265) calls loadConfig() as its merge base and writeJson's the public layer and credentials back (lines 255-263), so the next settings change permanently persists the reset and destroys the corrupt original. Refutation attempts failed: no other read path, backup, or guard exists for these files (grep over apps/desktop/src shows readJson only in config.js), and no quarantine/corrupt handling exists anywhere in apps/desktop. console.error is the established early-error channel in desktop main (apps/desktop/src/main/index.js:779).
verdicts.fix_plan: Root-cause fix in apps/desktop/src/main/config.js readJson only (no shim, no Config field — this is an app module, not a cordis plugin, and no deployment-varying tunable is introduced): (1) inside the try, read+parse as today; (2) catch with an error parameter and branch on `error.code === 'ENOENT'` → return `{ ...fallback }` with a comment naming the swallow ('first launch, no stored file yet'); (3) any other failure (JSON.parse SyntaxError, EACCES, EISDIR) → best-effort quarantine: `try { fs.renameSync(file, `${file}.corrupt-${Date.now()}`) } catch (renameError) { console.error(...naming rename failure...) }` then `console.error(`config: ${path.basename(file)} is unreadable (${error.message}); quarantined to <quarantine path>; continuing with defaults`)`, then return `{ ...fallback }`. Each catch names what it swallows and keeps one statement per try per the repo rule. Quarantine is what makes the fix root-cause rather than cosmetic: without it, the next saveConfig overwrites the corrupt file and the user's bytes are unrecoverable; with it the original survives alongside the regenerated defaults. Add a one-sentence JSDoc on readJson stating the contract: missing file falls back silently, unreadable existing file fails loud to stderr and is quarantined before fallback. No desktop README change needed — grep shows apps/desktop/README.md does not document config.json/credentials.json.
verdicts.risk: Behavior changes only on the corrupt-file path: the app still boots with defaults (boot resilience preserved — quarantining must be best-effort so a rename failure never blocks startup), but the loss is now visible on stderr (captured by terminal/boot logs) and the original bytes are preserved for manual recovery. The ENOENT path is unchanged, so first-launch and test environments are unaffected. The only new surface is the `.corrupt-<ts>` sibling files accumulating in userData — acceptable for a rare corruption event; if undesired, cap retention in a follow-up rather than complicating this fix.
verdicts.test_plan: apps/desktop/src/main/config.test.js (existing colocated node:test file that already stubs electron's app.getPath via require.cache and shares the userData tmpdir): add two cases — write invalid JSON to `<userData>/config.json`, call loadConfig(), assert it does not throw, returns a DEFAULTS-shaped config, and that `fs.readdirSync(userData)` contains an entry starting with 'config.json.corrupt-'; repeat for credentials.json asserting a 'credentials.json.corrupt-' entry and that loadConfig's credential fields fall back without throwing. Fails today: no quarantine file is created and nothing distinguishes the corrupt read. Filter quarantine assertions by prefix since the file's tests share one userData directory.

verdicts.fix_plan: 单文件修复（packages/storage/storage-sqlite/src/schema.ts），完整镜像兄弟协议：(1) 新增 `export const STORAGE_SQLITE_APPLICATION_ID = 0x44534852`（紧随 0x44534850/51 的既有序列，grep 确认无冲突；协议常量按 AGENTS.md 保持固定，不进 Config）。(2) configureDatabase 在任何 CREATE/PRAGMA 写操作之前：读 `PRAGMA application_id` 与 `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT GLOB 'sqlite_*'`；applicationId≠0 且≠ours → StorageError('version-mismatch' 之外新增语义化 code，如 'foreign-medium'，沿用 StorageError 既有构造形态)；applicationId=0 且 userTables 非空 → 拒绝（外来内容）；applicationId=ours → 校验 user tables ⊆ {units, unit_globals}，缺失即拒绝。(3) 新建库在现有『最后打戳』位置（:102-107）同时 `PRAGMA application_id = STORAGE_SQLITE_APPLICATION_ID` 和 user_version。(4) 预发布立场允许拒绝旧格式（AGENTS.md：Backends reject old on-disk formats），本包自己建的库修后重开也带新戳，无需迁移路径。(5) 更新 :31-35 的 jscpd 注释：镜像补全后注释成立，改写为指明三个 SQLite 后端共享同一 open/所有权序列。(6) README（packages/storage/storage-sqlite/README.md）补一句所有权拒绝语义；附 Agent Note（行为变化）。

verdicts.corrections: 行号核对：TS 418-420（performClose 早退）与 369-385（subscribe born-fail 条件）均仍准确；Python 143-146 与 696-704 均仍准确。影响面修正：高层 RelayHarness/HarnessSession.run 不受影响（订阅发生在 await start() 之后），暴露面是直接使用 HarnessClient.subscribe/subscribeSessionTree 的低层消费者；Python 侧同样是 HarnessClient 低层面。

verdicts.evidence: packages/host/apiproxy/src/frame-queue.ts:13-33 — `FrameQueue.push` does `this.buffer.push(item)` with no cap, no watermark, and no drop/disconnect policy; `end()` exists but nothing in the class ever calls it on growth. packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:2835-2836 creates one FrameQueue per events.mux subscriber and registers it in `muxQueues` (line 479); the per-subscriber `ctx.on('session/event')` listener at lines 2879-2897 pushes EVERY session event (high-frequency assistant deltas, tool events, views included) into that queue unconditionally, and `broadcast` (lines 620-624) pushes to every queue in muxQueues. packages/host/apiproxy/src/fetch/handler.ts:203-236 — sseResponse's `for await` loop calls `controller.enqueue` without ever consulting `desiredSize`, so enqueue never applies backpressure and the host pulls from the queue as fast as events arrive. The queue is removed from muxQueues only in iterate's cleanup (api-proxy.ts:2932-2935), which runs when the generator finishes — an aborted consumer does clean up (signal abort → end() → finally), but a connected-but-stalled consumer (TCP zero window, suspended proxy) never aborts and never pulls: the listener keeps pushing, the queue grows without bound for the stream's lifetime, and the dead queue also stays registered in muxQueues so every future event is retained. drain at frame-queue.ts:47 uses `buffer.shift()`, O(n) per frame. No bound exists anywhere on this path (grep for highWaterMark/desiredSize/maxQueued/overflow in apiproxy src hits only session-export.ts, which is the export download stream, not the mux stream — and that file's ResponseCapacityGate at session-export.ts:278-302 is the repo's own precedent for the fix shape). The client side is safe to terminate: packages/client/connection/src/client/connection.ts:176-202 — pumpStream's for-await ending calls settle → ac.abort() → recover() → reconnect with backoff, and events.mux reopen replays the full baseline (api-proxy.ts:2837-2873: session/subscribed per session, pending questions/approvals with stable rpcIds, queue snapshot, jobs baseline), so ending the queue on overflow loses no state. Corrections to the audit text: (1) 'muxQueues 中的死队列也不会被清理' is imprecise — aborted/closed queues ARE removed via the iterate cleanup; only stalled-but-open consumers leak their queue. (2) Line numbers drifted: push is now frame-queue.ts:23-27, shift at :47, the event listener at api-proxy.ts:2879-2897, queue creation at :2835, cleanup at :2932-2935, sseResponse at handler.ts:203-236.
verdicts.fix_plan: Root-cause fix in the owning module frame-queue.ts, no shims. (1) Bound the queue at its retention point: FrameQueue gains a constructor option `maxBytes: number` and tracks a running byte total; push() measures the frame with JSON.stringify(item) (the SSE layer serializes the same frame anyway, so this is the one honest measure of the retained value — AGENTS.md 'apply bounds to the complete result'), and when total exceeds maxBytes it calls end() instead of buffering: overflow terminates the subscriber stream, it never drops or truncates individual frames (a silently dropped delta would corrupt the client's incremental fold; termination is safe because the client reconnects and re-baselines, connection.ts:176-202 + mux reopen replay at api-proxy.ts:2837-2873). Document this contract in the class JSDoc. (2) Replace the buffer.shift() drain with a head index (`head` cursor advanced in iterate, buffer reset when drained) to kill the O(n²). (3) Config per the no-hardcoded-tunables rule: export DEFAULT_MUX_STREAM_BUFFER_BYTES from frame-queue.ts; add `muxStreamBufferBytes?: number` to Config + static Config (`z.natural().default(DEFAULT_MUX_STREAM_BUFFER_BYTES)`) in packages/host/apiproxy/src/index.ts (same shape as coldBlankProbeMaxBytes, lines 62/80), add the field with JSDoc to ApiProxyDefaults in api-proxy.ts, thread it through createApiProxy into both FrameQueue constructions (events.mux at :2835 and events.host at :2939). Misconfiguration (negative/non-integer) fails loud at load via the existing zod Config validation. (4) README: under Known Limitations and Deferred Work in packages/host/apiproxy/README.md, state the per-subscriber buffer bound and that a subscriber exceeding it is disconnected and served by client reconnect+baseline replay (folds into the same README pass as backlog item 19).
verdicts.test_plan: New packages/host/apiproxy/tests/frame-queue.spec.ts (package-level tests/ dir, matching existing naming). Failing-first case 1: construct FrameQueue with a tiny maxBytes, start iterate() with an abort controller and a cleanup spy, await one yielded frame, then push a frame whose serialized size exceeds the budget — assert the generator returns (iteration ends), cleanup ran exactly once, and a later push is a no-op. Today push never ends the queue, so this test times out/fails before the fix. Case 2: push N frames then drain — assert yields arrive in push order and the internal buffer is actually released (head-pointer behavior, observable via no shift-order regression). Integration pin (can ride the same spec or a new tests/api-proxy-mux.spec.ts using a real createApiProxy, not fakeApi): open events.mux, hold the consumer without pulling while the session emits events past the configured bound, assert the SSE response completes within a bounded time and a subsequent stream receives the full baseline (proves reconnect semantics). Update packages/host/apiproxy/tests/api-proxy-config.spec.ts for the new Config field default/validation.
verdicts.risk: Behavior change: a stalled or slow SSE subscriber is now disconnected (clean stream end) instead of accumulating unbounded host memory. Blast radius is contained by the client contract: every shipped client (connection.ts pumpStream) already treats stream end as reconnect-and-rebaseline, and the mux reopen replays subscriptions, pending questions/approvals, queue snapshots, and jobs baselines, so no event data is lost — worst case is a reconnect cycle for a genuinely slow-but-alive consumer. verdicts.title: session.list cold-summary batch is all-or-nothing: one bad cold log 500s the entire browse
verdicts.evidence: The cited aggregation shape exists — packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:1142-1153 collects Promise.allSettled results and `if (rejected) throw failure` — but the claimed trigger (a corrupt or half-written cold artifact causing a batch rejection) cannot reach that throw in current code: every realistic per-row failure is already caught and degraded per-row. The probe that reads a cold log, probeColdSessionMetadata in packages/host/apiproxy/src/session-list.ts:112-141, catches the stat failure (lines 125-130, returns undefined) and catches readFrom failure (lines 132-140: `ctx.logger.warn('session.list: blank probe for "<id>" failed (serving it as visible)')` then returns undefined), so a corrupt or torn artifact yields a visible row with a warning, not a rejection — this hardening is commit 2be3e12965 'fix(apiproxy): harden cold session metadata probing'. The other calls in the batch callback are equally safe: listProjectionsFor (api-proxy.ts:293-303) is fail-soft with its own warn; persistence.locate is pure path computation that touches no I/O (session-persistence-jsonl/src/index.ts:172-174; sqlite returns a constant, session-persistence-sqlite/src/index.ts:93); summarizeCold's remaining work (sessionListFields → resolveSessionPreset over header only, agent-presets/src/session.ts:48-54; sessionListUpdatedAt) is pure over already-validated durable headers; the re-attach branch (api-proxy.ts:1134-1135) only folds in-memory typed state. Torn tails are repaired by the persistence coordinator rather than thrown (per the session-storage slice's audited crash-repair sequencing). The only rejection that can reach `throw failure` today is request abort: signal?.throwIfAborted() (session-list.ts:120/123/134/137) propagates AbortError through the batch — where failing the request is moot (the client is gone) and arguably the desired early exit. Corrupt-store listing failure via persistence.list(signal) at api-proxy.ts:1115 also fails the whole call, but that is before and independent of the batching, and a wholly unreadable store failing the list loudly matches AGENTS.md fail-loud. So the claimed blast radius ('browse list permanently 500s until manual deletion') does not hold; the per-row degradation the finding asked for is already implemented and consistent with listProjectionsFor's documented posture.
verdicts.corrections: What survives is only a structurally all-or-nothing residue reachable solely via client abort: the rejected/failure loop at api-proxy.ts:1142-1153. That is not a bug — abort must propagate — and at most deserves a one-line comment naming why the aggregate throw is abort-only. No behavior change is warranted.
verdicts.fix_plan: No code change required. Optional zero-risk cleanup inside the same function: replace the `rejected`/`failure` first-failure loop (api-proxy.ts:1142-1153) with a direct scan that rethrows only when the rejection is an abort — e.g. keep the loop but add a comment stating the invariant 'a per-row rejection is abort; real row failures are degraded to visible rows in summarizeCold/probeColdSessionMetadata' — or simply leave the code as-is and fold a sentence into the README Known Limitations cold-path bullet confirming corrupt cold logs degrade to visible rows with a warning. verdicts.test_plan: Optional regression pin in the existing packages/host/apiproxy/tests/api-proxy-cold.spec.ts (it already owns cold-list behavior): a case where persistence.readFrom rejects with a non-abort error for one cold session (inject a persistence stub whose readFrom throws for a chosen id) and asserts session.list still returns 200 with that session present, blank:true, and the other rows intact. verdicts.evidence: Current code confirms every claim. `store` is declared at packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts:102 and entries are deleted in exactly two places: `disposeOwned` (line 471, fired by the owner agent's scope effect registered in ensureOwnerCleanup, line 459-463) and `disposeAll` (line 494 `store.clear()`, service teardown). `settle()` (lines 416-440) records the terminal outcome but never deletes; `read()`, `kill()`, and `wait()` only set `reported` (lines 211, 219, 277) and nothing consumes that flag for retention. `list()` (lines 192-197) returns every stored record owner-filtered with no terminal pruning, and it is the model-facing surface: packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:356 calls `ctx.jobs.list(exec.agent)` for the model's job list, and line 189 uses it for output-limit resolution. `JobStart.owner` is optional (packages/jobs/jobs/src/types.ts:62, JSDoc: 'Omitting the owner creates an unowned job'), and `disposeOwned` filters `job.owner === owner` (index.ts:468), so unowned rows have no deletion path before service teardown. The jobs-local README has no retention contract (grep for retention/prune/terminal-record terms returns nothing), so this is not a documented intentional trade-off. The existing test only pins bounded wait-resolver retention while a job is live (tests/jobs.spec.ts:106-110 waitResolverCount helper), not store growth.
verdicts.corrections: Two precision notes. (1) Line drift: the audit cited jobs.spec.ts:105; the wait-resolver helper now sits at tests/jobs.spec.ts:106-110. (2) For owned jobs the leak is bounded by the owning agent's lifetime (owner scope disposal cancels, awaits settlement, and deletes the rows) — the unbounded-growth case is long-lived agents and, absolutely, unowned jobs. The `reported` flag already exists and is maintained on every terminal path (read/kill/wait/settle/teardown), which makes it the natural retention signal; the fix needs no new state.
verdicts.fix_plan: Root-cause fix in LocalJobRegistry only, no shims. (1) Add two validated Config fields to `Config` + `LocalJobRegistry.Config` (schemastery, following the existing maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner pattern at index.ts:92-98): `terminalRetentionMs` (positive safe integer, default 60_000) and `maxTerminalRecords` (positive safe integer, default 100). (2) Add a private `pruneTerminal(now)` sweep: a record is prunable iff `isTerminal(status) && reported && finishedAt !== undefined && now - finishedAt >= terminalRetentionMs`; delete prunable records, enforce `maxTerminalRecords` per owner-bucket (owner id, or the shared unowned bucket) by dropping oldest-finishedAt beyond the cap, and call `notifyChanged(owner)` for each affected owner (mirroring the removal-announcement comment at index.ts:472-474). Never prune an unreported terminal record — that preserves at-least-once completion-notice semantics. (3) Invoke `pruneTerminal(Date.now())` at the top of `start()` and `list()` — both already traverse the store; no timer, no background task. (4) `expect()` already fails loud for pruned ids (`unknown job ${id}`, index.ts:347), so job_output of a pruned id fails loud with no new code. (5) JSDoc: document the retention contract on the class (records retained until terminal + reported + grace/cap; a pruned id reads as unknown job) and mirror it in the Service Definition JSDoc in packages/jobs/jobs/src plus the jobs-local README. Write the Agent Note for the behavior change per repo policy.
verdicts.risk: Behavior change: a caller reading a job after terminal + reported + grace (or beyond the cap) now gets `unknown job <id>` instead of the stale snapshot; jobs list output shrinks. Safety hinges on the reported gate — the completion notice has already been delivered before pruning can occur, so no notice is lost. Keep defaults generous, document the window, and only sweep on start/list (O(store), no hot-path cost). No wire or persistence format impact: the store is in-memory and per-process.

verdicts.title: CircuitBreaker half-open accounting lets stale closed-state outcomes consume probe slots and close the breaker early
verdicts.evidence: Current code confirms the accounting defect. `check()` in the closed branch returns immediately without claiming anything (packages/guard/llm-circuit-breaker/src/breaker.ts:48-49), so closed-admitted requests have no probe slot. `record()` in half-open unconditionally `this.probes.shift()`s and then trips on failure or closes on success (breaker.ts:81-85). A request admitted while closed that settles after the trip — specifically after some later `check()` transitioned open→half-open (breaker.ts:55-58) — lands in that branch: a stale success calls `close()` (line 84) before any genuine probe outcome, and a stale failure calls `trip()` (line 83) even though the real probe might have succeeded. Wired per provider at packages/guard/llm-circuit-breaker/src/index.ts:94-117 (`agent/request` check, `agent/request-error` record-failure, `session/event` assistant/message record-success), so every provider request is exposed. Samples have no count cap: `evict()` (breaker.ts:112-118) removes only samples older than windowMs (default 60s, index.ts:37), so a high-rate window accumulates the whole window's outcomes. Existing tests (tests/breaker.spec.ts:29-54) only exercise genuine probe claims and outcomes; no stale-admission case exists.
verdicts.corrections: Two sharpening corrections. (1) The window is narrower than 'any post-trip settlement': while the breaker is 'open', record() is a no-op (breaker.ts:79-80); the stale outcome only misaccounts if it arrives during the half-open phase, i.e. after openMs elapsed and a new check() ran. (2) A stale failure does not consume a slot — `trip()` clears probes entirely (breaker.ts:120-124); its harm is force-reopening on an outcome that never measured recovery, extending the outage by another openMs. The stale-success case is the worse half: it closes the breaker with zero genuine probe evidence. The success path is structurally exposed because session/event assistant/message records success for every completed request, including bulk traffic admitted just before the trip. Correlation keys for a fix exist at all three sites: `agent/request` payload has {agent, turn, step} (packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts:244), `agent/request-error` has {agent, turn, step, provider} (runtime-types.ts:260), assistant/message events carry {turn, step} plus message.source.provider, and Session exposes `id: SessionId` (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:441) with `Agent.session` available (runtime-types.ts:70).
verdicts.fix_plan: (1) breaker.ts — make admission explicit: `check(now)` returns an admission token `{ admittedIn: 'closed' } | { admittedIn: 'half-open' }` (closed branch and the open→half-open transition each return their token); `record(token, failed, now)` in the half-open branch routes by the token: a closed-admitted token pushes to `samples` + evicts only, never shifting a probe and never calling trip/close from it; a half-open token keeps the current shift/trip/close behavior; an undefined token (defensive) is treated as closed-admitted. Closed-state accounting is unchanged. JSDoc both methods with the token contract (@param/@returns per repo rule). (2) index.ts — correlate tokens: after `await next()` resolves the provider in `agent/request`, run `check()` and store the token in a Map keyed `${provider}�${agent.session.id}�${turn}�${step}`; `agent/request-error` and the assistant/message `session/event` handler look up by the same key, delete the entry, and pass the token to `record()`. Bound the map with a new validated Config field `maxInflightAdmissions` (positive safe integer, default 1000): on overflow evict the oldest entry with a `ctx.logger.warn` naming the provider (attempts can legitimately be long, so eviction-plus-warn rather than throw). (3) Sample cap: add `maxSamples` to CircuitBreakerPolicy and a Config field (positive safe integer, default 1000); `evict()` drops oldest beyond the cap, bounding closed-state memory. (4) Update the package README Known Limitations/contract text: bulk outcomes admitted before a trip never settle probes and no longer close or reopen the breaker.
verdicts.risk: Pre-release stance allows the check()/record() signature change; the only callers are index.ts and the package tests, all updated in the same PR. Behavior moves strictly in the safe direction: stale bulk outcomes can no longer close the breaker without probe evidence or reopen it on an unmeasured failure; recovery latency now depends only on genuine probes. New state is one bounded Map entry per in-flight attempt, deleted on first outcome, capped by config. No wire, session-log, or snapshot impact (model-visible text unchanged — LlmError message only fires on open).
verdicts.test_plan: Extend packages/guard/llm-circuit-breaker/tests/breaker.spec.ts (existing convention). Failing-first case: trip the breaker, advance now past openMs, `check()` claims a probe, then `record(closedToken, false, now)` — before the fix this closes the breaker (state === 'closed'); after the fix state stays 'half-open', the probe slot is intact (a second check() still throws CircuitBreakerOpenError at halfOpenMaxProbes=1), and only `record(halfOpenToken, false, now)` closes. Companion case: `record(closedToken, true, now)` in half-open does NOT trip. Add a samples-cap case (maxSamples exceeded drops oldest without changing errorRate semantics) and a plugin-level case in tests/plugin.spec.ts asserting the admission map entry is deleted after an outcome and the overflow path evicts oldest with a warn.

findings.risk: A bound turns an oversized stored payload into a loud CodeIndexError (already the package's failure mode for undecodable payloads); choose the bound from the indexer's own chunk cap so legitimate rows never trip it. findings.title: Persistence write path relies on a Cordis teardown-ordering guarantee the framework does not provide: cross-effect disposal is concurrent (Promise.all), so 'event admission closes before the drain' holds only by microtask-scheduling accident
findings.evidence: packages/session/session-persistence/src/coordinator.ts:1090-1092 documents the invariant as framework-provided: 'Cordis tears effects down in reverse registration order, so event admission closes before this final drain reaches quiescence and closes the backend.' But the drain disposer (coordinator.ts:1093, ctx.effect) and each of the four ctx.on listeners (coordinator.ts:1119-1134) are SEPARATE top-level effects — every ctx.on registers its own effect (vendor/cordis/src/events.ts:254-260) — and the vendored fiber disposes all top-level effects of a fiber CONCURRENTLY: `await Promise.all(this._disposables.clear().map(...))` (vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:675-686). Reverse registration order is only honored sequentially WITHIN one effect group (fiber.ts:427-442 builds the sequential reversed chain per group). Today the invariant still holds, but only because every listener removal is synchronous and each composeError callback yields exactly one microtask, so the removals (reversed array, equal microtask depth) complete before the drain wrapper's extra await chain reaches its flush body. Any future async disposer in that fiber (or any removal path that yields before unregistering) reopens the window: a session/event enqueued after the drain captured [...this.live.keys()] (coordinator.ts:1096) and after that session's flush joined/settled its barrier arms a plain 200ms setTimeout (packages/session/session-persistence/src/write-behind.ts:45-56, 81-83; DEFAULT_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=200, coordinator.ts:31). The drain then closes the backend in its finally (coordinator.ts:1104-1114); when the timer fires, startWrite writes against the closed backend, the failure is retained in pending and only reported via reportBackgroundFailure → logger.warn (write-behind.ts:145-152; coordinator.ts:1353-1355). The dispose effect itself reports success (no error), so model-visible events are silently never persisted — violating model-visible ⟺ logged — with a single warn as the only trace.
findings.fix_plan: Make the ordering structural instead of scheduler-dependent, using the ordering Cordis actually guarantees (within one effect group): convert installWritePath's registration into one composite generator effect — `ctx.effect(function* () { yield listenerCreated; yield listenerEvent; yield listenerFlush; yield listenerDisposed; return async () => { ...existing drain + backend.close()... } })` — so the four listener disposers are children of the drain's group and Cordis's sequential reverse chain (fiber.ts:427-442) removes them before the drain body runs, deterministically. As belt-and-braces, set a `this.tearingDown = true` flag as the drain body's first statement and have the session/event listener treat it as admission-closed (skip enqueue, matching the existing disposed-fence containment) so even an out-of-order removal cannot strand a batch past backend.close(). Update the comment at coordinator.ts:1090-1092 to name the real mechanism (composite effect, not global reverse order).
findings.test_plan: In packages/session/session-persistence/tests (coordinator spec with a fake backend): (1) failing-first probe of the assumption — register an extra same-fiber effect whose disposer awaits a tick before removing its session/event listener (simulating the future async removal); make backend.append gate on a deferred; call dispose of the fiber; while the drain is blocked, append one event to the live session; release the gate; await dispose. Assert the appended event IS durably stored (or its loss is loud via the dispose AggregateError). On current code the event lands in a post-close timer batch and is only warned — the assertion fails (red). (2) After the composite-effect fix, the same scenario passes and additionally asserts `session/event` dispatch has zero listeners by the time the drain's first flush begins (observable via a probe listener counter).

findings.title: A failed session retirement permanently strands the coordinator's live entry and blocks reuse of that session id until process exit: no retry path exists between the fire-and-forget session/disposed retire and coordinator dispose
findings.evidence: Session disposal is observe-only and fire-and-forget: `ctx.on('session/disposed', session => { this.retire(session) })` (coordinator.ts:1134); the store's emitDisposed contains listener failures and never awaits them (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:1063-1072). retire() → retireCore awaits `this.flush(session)` first (coordinator.ts:1156-1157); if that flush rejects (one transient backend append failure — startWrite re-retains the batch, sets automaticPaused, and rethrows; write-behind.ts:145-152), retire only logs `retirement failed` and forgets the promise (coordinator.ts:1150-1152). `this.live.delete(session)` at coordinator.ts:1160 is the ONLY deletion site of the live map, and it never runs, so the stranded SessionWriteBehind (with its retained pending events) is kept for the process lifetime. There is no retry: the disposed session is out of the SessionStore, and `sessions.flush` requires a live entry (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:1088, liveEntryFor) — nothing can reach the stuck controller. Concurrently, id reuse now fails forever: onCreated's collision branch (coordinator.ts:1267-1272) sees `tracked.owner` = the disposed session, `owner.writes.hasWork` is true (pending retained, write-behind.ts:36-38), so any create/resume of that id throws 'session "X" is already bound to a different live session in this backend (id collision)' — this hits real consumers, e.g. subagent continuation resume by childId (packages/subagent/subagent/src/continuation.ts:1250-1264). `waitForRetirement` (coordinator.ts:994) is awaited only by the coordinator's own create/inspect paths (lines 723, 759, 791) and retirements were already deleted by `forget`; no lifecycle owner (AgentHandle.dispose in packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:534-557, ACP quiesce in packages/acp/acp/src/index.ts:493) ever awaits retirement durability. The stranded batch surfaces only if the coordinator's dispose effect later flushes the still-live entry (coordinator.ts:1096).
findings.fix_plan: Give a failed retirement a bounded, loud recovery instead of a warn-and-strand. Minimal change in retire(): on flush failure, keep the retirement entry in `this.retirements` as a rejected-but-retryable record and (a) arm one retry (e.g. re-run retireCore after a backoff, still warn-contained), and (b) make the id-collision branch cooperate: in onCreated case 1, when `tracked.owner`'s live entry exists but its Session is disposed (retirement previously failed), await a fresh `flush` attempt on that stranded controller; if it succeeds, reclaim exactly as the `!materialized && !hasWork` arm does (delete live + states, proceed with creation); if it fails again, rethrow the ORIGINAL write error (loud, naming the stuck id) instead of the misleading 'bound to a different live session' collision text.
findings.test_plan: In packages/session/session-persistence/tests with the existing fake-backend harness: (1) failing-first — backend.append rejects exactly once; create session S, append an event, dispose S (store detach), await a tick; then create a new live session with S's id. On current code this throws the id-collision error and the pending batch is never re-attempted — assert instead that the create either succeeds after the retry drains the batch (backend then contains S's events plus the new seed) or rejects with the original write failure; the collision text assertion documents the red state. (2) Companion case: retry exhaustion — append always fails; create(same id) must reject with the write error naming the id, the stranded entry must be released (subsequent create still fails loud but memory is dropped), and `dispose` of the coordinator must not double-report. Also add the mirror behavior test for the subagent continuation path only if the seam-level fix changes its error surface.

slices.changes: config.js readJson(:180-186):try 内照常读+parse;catch 带 error 参数,`error.code === 'ENOENT'` → 返回 {...fallback} 并注释命名吞没('first launch, no stored file yet');其他失败(JSON.parse SyntaxError/EACCES/EISDIR)→ best-effort `fs.renameSync(file, `${file}.corrupt-${Date.now()}`)` 隔离(rename 失败自身 console.error 且不阻塞启动),`console.error('config: <basename> is unreadable (<msg>); quarantined to <path>; continuing with defaults')`,再回退 defaults;readJson 加一句 JSDoc 契约(缺文件静默回退,已存在不可读先响亮+隔离)。隔离是根因修复的关键:没有它下一次 saveConfig 会覆盖坏文件使用户字节不可恢复。rlh.js:(1) ensureOwnedPort(:397-407)删除 probe.httpReady→killOwnedListeners 块,pid-file 尝试后占用端口直接走既有 findFreePort hop,JSDoc 契约改为'只杀 rlhd-web.pid 记录且 isSafeToKill 的 pid,其余监听者一律跳端口';(2) _doStop(:908-912)删除无条件 killOwnedListeners sweep 及日志,路径本就只杀 child?.pid || pidFile;(3) 删除死代码 listeningPids(:250-282)、killOwnedListeners(:284-298)及 RlhManager deps 表项(:463/:491/:961-963);(4) spawnHarness(:314-322)POSIX 传 detached:true 使子进程自 lead 进程组,killTree 的 process.kill(-pid) 真正覆盖整树(Windows taskkill /T /F 不变);无新 Config 字段(port 已是 config.port)。
slices.tests: rlh.test.js(node:test + deps 注入)failing-first:(1) 新用例'外部 node 监听不被击杀,跳端口'——注入 stale pid file(processAlive=false)+ 200 响应 + 外来监听 pid 9999(image 'node'),断言返回端口 > wanted 且 killTree 未以外来 pid 调用(现实现 httpReady 分支会杀,先红);(2) 重写 :420 stop 用例:断言 stop 路径不再 sweep 端口(去掉 calls.killOwned,仅 killTree:[CHILD_PID];现实现为 1,先红);(3) spawnHarness 在 POSIX 传 detached:true 的纯断言。config.test.js(共享 userData tmpdir,按前缀过滤断言):写坏 JSON 到 <userData>/config.json → loadConfig 不抛、返回 DEFAULTS 形状、readdir 出现 'config.json.corrupt-' 前缀条目;credentials.json 同理且凭据字段回退不抛。
slices.docs: 无 README 面(apps/desktop/README.md 未记载 config.json/端口击杀语义,grep 已核实);.agents/notes/ Agent Note(端口冲突从击杀变为跳端口的行为变更)。

plan.strategy: R5(后端优化)共 10 个 slice,按 severity→effort 排序:high 段(hooks 循环护栏、apiproxy FrameQueue、SDK 会话回收 TS/Python、jobs 保留、SQLite 束)在前,medium 段按 effort 升序(atomic-write S → persistence teardown/spill M → desktop L)在后。同包编辑全部合并以避免冲突:R5-B 收拢 apiproxy 三项(FrameQueue + preset 切换 TOCTOU + 冷探测复核);R5-C/R5-D 按 TS/协议与 Python 语言边界切分 SDK 工作并保持 C→D 依赖序(Python session_close 需要 R5-C 的协议方法),两 slice 不共改同一文件;R5-F 合并 session-query-sqlite 与 storage-sqlite;R5-J 合并 desktop 两项;R5-I 合并 subprocess/spill 双包同主题。新维度发现的取舍:teardown-drain 两项(R5-H)、spill 两项(R5-I)、agentPresets.select TOCTOU 与冷探测 TOCTOU(并入 R5-B)全部纳入;延后至 R6+:R1 rank 12(agent-loop 空 enter 搁置输入,S)、rank 16(CircuitBreaker half-open 记账,M)、新维度 T/U(zstd 解压上限,low)、W(agentPresets.copy 并发 rm,low)。Refuted 处理:R1 rank 18(session.list 冷摘要 500)整体 refuted,无行为修改,仅随 R5-B 的 README pass 补一句降级语义,已在 R5-B.refuted 列明;R1 rank 1 的 hooks-codex 半边 refuted(护栏已上线),已在 R5-A.refuted 列明。每个 slice 均含 failing-first 测试、同 PR README/JSDoc 更新;非平凡行为变更(hooks 护栏、mux 断开、SDK 生命周期、所有权拒绝、锁自愈、spill 降级、端口击杀收敛、退休重试)按 AGENTS.md 附 Agent Note;快照面变化(R5-C finishReason)同 PR 更新两套 expected-output。
